strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer vision problem: generating complementary 3D assets while preserving an input mesh and recovering coherent object–object relationships. Using a generated scene as spatial guidance rather than directly segmenting it into final assets is a sensible design.

The pipeline coherently combines global-to-local registration, collision-aware pose refinement, and image-based geometry correction. Figures 6 and 10 show convincing examples of improved alignment and preservation of individual asset geometry.

On the 10 evaluated cases, Table 2 reports improvements across all four metrics. Relative to PartField+RANSAC, volumetric intersection decreases from 6.7744 to 3.2467 × 10⁻³, while text CLIP increases from 0.3129 to 0.3307.

The supplementary material provides multi-view examples, multi-object compositions, and informative failure cases involving geometric symmetry and unreliable scene guidance. The proposed dataset could be useful if adequately documented and released.
weaknesses: The quantitative evidence is insufficient for the claimed robustness and scalability. Section 5.3 evaluates only 10 illustrated cases, without a sampling protocol, variability estimates, category breakdowns, or quantitative multi-object evaluation. This is particularly limiting given the approximately 8,300 scenes claimed in Appendix A.1.

There are no component ablations. The experiments do not isolate anchor selection, GeoTransformer initialization, SDF refinement, the penalty schedule, or agentic correction. The agentic component is supported by two qualitative examples, without aggregate success rates or comparison against unguided regeneration. Consequently, the contribution of the proposed mechanisms remains unclear.

Baseline comparisons have important confounds. Jigsaw and 2BY2 receive neither the additional semantic guidance nor scale optimization available to Interact3D, and Jigsaw targets fractured-object assembly. PartField+RANSAC is informative but does not isolate improvements over the same registration pipeline without collision refinement. Closely related text-guided composition work, COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE, is discussed but not evaluated.

The claims of physically sound, simulation-ready interaction exceed the evidence. Equations (2)–(3) penalize sampled penetration but do not enforce support, stable contact, gravity, or functional interaction. Repulsion can also introduce gaps. CLIP and intersection ratios cannot establish these properties, and no physical simulation validation is provided. Nonzero residual intersections in Table 2 further qualify the collision-free language.

The dataset contribution is underdocumented. Beyond approximate scene counts and stored meshes/poses, the manuscript does not establish asset provenance and redistribution permissions, category coverage, duplicate handling, filtering criteria, generation yield, or independent quality validation. Its scale alone does not establish its suitability for downstream research.

Reproducibility and practical scalability remain uncertain. Missing details include SDF construction and resolution, safety margin, point sampling and coordinate normalization, optimization settings, segmentation-to-object association, and the complete agent prompting and stopping protocol. Runtime, hardware, API cost, and refinement frequency are also absent. The surface-intersection metric needs a precise definition of intersected area, since triangle intersections generally form curves. Overall, the integration is promising, but these evidence gaps prevent a convincing acceptance case under Algorithms/General.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer-vision problem: generating separate, geometrically compatible objects while preserving a user-provided asset. Using a generated scene as spatial guidance rather than directly segmenting it into final assets is a sensible design.

The pipeline coherently combines global-to-local registration, SDF-based collision penalties, and image-based geometry refinement. Figures 6 and 10 show visible improvements over the evaluated baselines, and the supplementary multi-view examples demonstrate promising asset quality.

Table 2 provides preliminary quantitative support: compared with PartField+RANSAC, surface intersection decreases from 2.1523 to 0.6766 × 10−3 and volumetric intersection from 6.7744 to 3.2467 × 10−3, alongside improved CLIP scores.

The proposed collection of approximately 8,300 compositional scenes could be useful. The discussion also acknowledges meaningful limitations, including symmetry-related orientation errors, inaccurate guidance geometry, and difficulty with tightly coupled components.
weaknesses: The experimental evidence is insufficient for the breadth of the claims. Section 5.3 evaluates only ten test cases, without a documented sampling protocol, repeated generations, uncertainty estimates, or per-case results. Despite the claimed dataset scale, there is no representative large-scale evaluation; multi-object scalability is supported primarily by illustrations.

There are no component ablations separating the effects of GeoTransformer initialization, scale-aware ICP, anchor selection, SDF optimization, and agentic refinement. In particular, the agentic contribution is demonstrated through two qualitative examples without aggregate success rates, comparison against unguided regeneration, or reporting of its contribution to Table 2. The necessity and reliability of the proposed components therefore remain unclear.

The baseline comparisons have substantial confounds. Jigsaw targets fractured-object assembly, while both Jigsaw and 2BY2 lack scale optimization and receive no image or text guidance. Their failures do not isolate the advantages of the proposed composition algorithm. PartField+RANSAC provides a more relevant comparison but changes registration and collision handling simultaneously. COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE, a closely related text-guided alignment method discussed in the paper, is not evaluated.

Reduced interpenetration does not establish the repeatedly claimed physical soundness or readiness for robotic simulation. Equation (2) penalizes penetration and encourages clearance but does not enforce support, stable contact, gravity, or functional compatibility. No simulation-based stability or interaction tests are provided. CLIP similarity and intersection ratios can both overlook floating or functionally incorrect placements.

The dataset contribution is underdocumented. Appendix A.1 gives approximate counts and asset types but no systematic category distribution, provenance and licensing details, duplicate analysis, quality-control protocol, or independent assessment of valid compositions. These omissions prevent judging whether the collection constitutes a reliable resource rather than simply a large set of pipeline outputs.

Important reproducibility and measurement details are missing: the SDF resolution and sign handling, point sampling, safety margin epsilon, numerical optimizer, CLIP backbone and evaluation views, and complete agent prompts and stopping criteria. The surface-intersection metric also needs clarification: generic triangle intersections are curves, so the definition of the reported intersected surface area is ambiguous. Runtime, API cost, and regeneration frequency are absent despite the scalability claim.

Assessed as Algorithms/General, the originality is mainly in integrating existing generators, registration methods, collision penalties, and VLM editing. Such integration can warrant acceptance, but here the missing controlled experiments and resource validation leave its incremental scientific contribution insufficiently established. The promising examples support further development, while the current evidence favors weak rejection.

Using an imperfect reconstructed scene as spatial guidance for independently generated meshes is a sensible design that avoids directly retaining segmentation holes.

Figures 6 and 10 show convincing improvements over the displayed baselines, while the supplementary multi-view examples demonstrate appealing asset quality across varied everyday objects.

In particular, the central refinement contribution is supported by illustrative examples rather than aggregate success rates, collision reduction, semantic preservation, or comparison against simply regenerating the complementary object. Under the default Algorithms/General category, the methodological advance beyond integrating existing components remains insufficiently established.

Jigsaw addresses fractured-object assembly, and both Jigsaw and 2BY2 lack the additional conditioning and scale optimization available to Interact3D. PartField+RANSAC is more comparable, but does not isolate registration improvements from collision handling. The closely related text-guided COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE method is discussed but not evaluated.

The objective lacks explicit support, contact, or stability constraints, and the evaluation includes no gravity-based stability or interaction tests. Collision ratios can improve through separation without achieving a valid functional relationship; CLIP similarity does not adequately resolve this ambiguity. Equation (2) is a finite, sampled penalty rather than a collision-free guarantee.

Appendix A.1 gives approximate counts and broad content descriptions, but no category distribution, source-asset provenance and licensing breakdown, filtering criteria, duplicate analysis, or independently assessed quality statistics. These omissions prevent assessing its diversity, reliability, and redistribution readiness.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer vision problem: generating complementary 3D objects while preserving an existing asset and its intended spatial relationships. The generate-then-compose formulation is sensible and avoids relying on incomplete segmented geometry as the final output.

The pipeline coherently combines generative scene guidance, global-to-local registration, collision-aware refinement, and corrective image editing. Figures 4 and 8 illustrate why modifying incompatible geometry can help when pose optimization alone is insufficient.

Results on 150 cases show consistent improvements over the reported baselines. Relative to PartField+RANSAC, the volumetric intersection ratio decreases from 0.007928 to 0.003876, and the human rating increases from 6.28 to 8.33. The agentic refinement ablation also improves all reported metrics.

The supplementary material provides extensive qualitative examples, multiple viewpoints, and explicit failure analysis. The proposed dataset of approximately 8,300 scenes across nine categories could be useful if its quality and provenance are established.
weaknesses: The central claims of physical soundness exceed the evidence. Equations (2)–(3) penalize sampled penetration but do not enforce support, stable contact, gravity, or functional interaction; soft penalties also do not guarantee collision-free geometry. No physics simulation or functional interaction evaluation is provided. Figure 7 reports 29 failures among 140 cases, approximately 21%, including 16 collision-induced divergences, which warrants substantially more qualification than claims of guaranteed or strict physical plausibility.

The comparisons do not adequately separate methodological improvements from privileged conditioning and task mismatch. Jigsaw and 2BY2 receive neither the image/text guidance nor scale optimization available to Interact3D, and Jigsaw targets fractured-object assembly. The more relevant text-guided COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE method is discussed but not evaluated. Stronger comparisons using identical generated assets, spatial guidance, and scale handling are needed.

The ablations do not isolate key contributions. Table 3 compares GeoTransformer alone against GeoTransformer+ICP(SDF), changing both local refinement and collision handling; it therefore does not substantiate the stated isolated effect of removing the SDF term. There is also no matched-budget regeneration baseline to determine whether targeted VLM feedback improves over simply retrying generation, nor an ablation of anchor selection or the two-stage design.

Evaluation protocols are insufficiently specified. The manuscript does not explain selection of the 150 cases, their relationship to the curated dataset, the number and expertise of human raters, rating instructions, agreement, or uncertainty. CLIP similarity and mean penetration ratios provide limited evidence of correct object relationships, particularly because separated or floating objects can have low penetration. Multi-object scalability is demonstrated qualitatively without quantitative analysis.

The dataset contribution remains underdocumented. Appendix A.1 reports approximately 8,300 scenes selected from 10,000 candidates, but gives no selection criteria, independent quality audit, detailed category distribution, diversity analysis, or clear source-asset provenance and licensing. These omissions prevent assessing whether the collection is a reliable resource beyond the showcased examples.

Reproduction and assessment of scalability require substantial missing details: SDF construction and resolution, surface sampling, safety margin, transformation optimization, VLM prompts and collision-trigger thresholds, model versions, and runtime/API costs. Since the algorithmic contribution largely integrates existing components, stronger controlled evidence and implementation detail are especially important. The current evidence establishes a promising pipeline but leaves consequential uncertainty about its distinct contribution and reliability.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer-vision problem: generating complementary objects while preserving separate, high-quality meshes and their spatial relationships. Using a reconstructed scene as registration guidance, rather than directly extracting its incomplete components, is a sensible design.

The integrated pipeline is technically plausible. Global-to-local registration supplies initialization, SDF penalties reduce interpenetration, and image-based regeneration can address geometric incompatibilities that pose optimization alone cannot resolve. Figures 4 and 8 illustrate the latter motivation clearly.

The reported results on 150 cases favor Interact3D across several complementary metrics. Relative to PartField+RANSAC, human ratings improve from 6.28 to 8.33 and volumetric intersection decreases from 7.9280 to 3.8762 × 10−3. The supplementary multi-view examples provide useful qualitative evidence of asset quality.

The approximately 8,300-scene dataset could be a useful resource. The supplementary material also discloses concrete failure modes, including symmetry ambiguity, reconstruction holes, and collision-induced divergence.
weaknesses: The central claims of physically sound interactive scenes exceed the evidence. Equations (2)–(3) penalize sampled interpenetration but do not enforce support, contact, gravitational stability, or interaction feasibility. Separated or floating objects can have zero intersection, and finite soft penalties do not guarantee collision-free geometry. No simulation or manipulation evaluation establishes the stronger claims, including the assertion in Figure 10 that the method guarantees physical plausibility. Such downstream experiments are not essential for a narrower geometric-composition contribution, but the current claims require stronger validation.

The comparisons do not adequately separate method quality from differences in available information and task suitability. Jigsaw and 2BY2 receive neither the image/text conditioning nor the generated scene guidance used by Interact3D, and cannot optimize scale; Jigsaw additionally targets fractured-object assembly. The RANSAC baseline is more controlled, but the paper does not compare with the text-guided composition method COPY-TRANSFORM-PASTE discussed in related work, or a similarly conditioned competitive alternative. Consequently, the broad superiority claims are insufficiently supported.

The ablations do not isolate key contributions. Table 3 moves from GeoTransformer alone to GeoTransformer+ICP(SDF), changing local refinement and collision handling together; it lacks GeoTransformer+ICP without SDF, despite the accompanying claim that removing the SDF term was evaluated. The agentic-loop ablation is informative, but an equal-budget regeneration or generic-feedback control is needed to establish the value of targeted VLM feedback beyond additional generation attempts.

Evaluation reliability is difficult to assess. The manuscript does not specify how the 150 cases were selected or their relationship to the curated dataset, and provides no human-rater counts, rating rubric, blinding procedure, agreement, or uncertainty estimates. Figure 7 reports 29 failures among 140 additional cases, approximately 21%, which deserves explicit reconciliation with the descriptions of robust performance and only a small fraction of failures. Aggregate CLIP and intersection averages do not explain how often compositions actually succeed.

The dataset contribution is underdocumented. Appendix A.1 states that approximately 8,300 scenes were selected from 10,000 candidates, but does not explain selection criteria, manual involvement, quality auditing, source-asset provenance and licensing, or the relationship between filtering and reported failures. There is no quantitative analysis of the approximately 600 multi-object scenes. These omissions limit confidence in both dataset quality and the claim of fully automated, scalable curation.

Important reproducibility and efficiency details are missing: SDF construction and resolution, safety margin ε, mesh sampling and normalization, optimizer settings, agent prompts and stopping criteria, and the treatment of non-watertight meshes in inside/outside tests. The surface-intersection metric also needs an operational definition of the area attributed to triangle–triangle intersections. Reporting a single H200 does not establish scalability without runtime, API cost, or refinement-iteration statistics.

Under the default Algorithms/General assessment, the originality is primarily the integration of existing generators, segmentation, registration, collision penalties, and VLM editing. Such integration can warrant publication, but here its significance depends heavily on controlled empirical validation and a reproducible resource. The missing controls and dataset documentation leave important concerns unresolved, supporting a weak-reject recommendation despite the promising examples.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer-vision problem: generating complementary objects while preserving an existing mesh and recovering meaningful spatial relationships. Using a reconstructed scene as spatial guidance, rather than as the final geometry, is a sensible way to avoid the holes and fused surfaces produced by direct segmentation.

The pipeline coherently combines global-to-local registration, collision-aware refinement, and image-based geometry correction. The agentic loop can address incompatible shapes that pose optimization alone cannot repair, as illustrated by the vase and teddy-bear examples.

Results on 150 cases show consistent improvements across the reported metrics. Relative to PartField+RANSAC, human ratings increase from 6.28 to 8.33 and volumetric intersection decreases from 7.9280 to 3.8762 × 10−3. The supplementary multi-view examples provide useful qualitative evidence of asset quality.

The proposed dataset of approximately 8,300 scenes across nine categories could be valuable. The manuscript also usefully discloses failures involving symmetry, reconstruction defects, and collision-induced divergence.
weaknesses: The central claims of physically sound scenes and guaranteed physical plausibility exceed the evidence. Equations (2)–(3) penalize sampled penetration but do not enforce support, stable contact, or equilibrium; separated or floating objects can have zero intersection. The positive safety margin can also encourage gaps. Figure 7 reports 29 failures among 140 examples, approximately 21%, including 16 collision-induced failures. This is meaningful evidence against the stronger guarantees, although it does not negate the demonstrated collision reduction.

The comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the contribution. Jigsaw and 2BY2 lack the image/text guidance and scale adjustment available to Interact3D, and Jigsaw addresses a substantially different assembly setting. More importantly, Table 3 lacks GeoTransformer+ICP without SDF, so the claimed SDF ablation also changes registration refinement. The agentic loop is not compared with an equal-budget regeneration baseline, leaving uncertainty about the benefit of targeted feedback versus additional generation attempts.

Evaluation protocols are insufficiently specified. The manuscript does not explain how the 150 cases were selected, their relationship to the curated dataset, the number of human raters, rating instructions, blinding, or uncertainty. Qwen3's exact configuration and evaluation prompts are absent. Image CLIP measures agreement with the pipeline's own generated guidance, which can reward inherited errors. The surface-intersection metric also needs a precise operational definition: intersecting triangles generally meet along curves, so the stated area could mean several different quantities.

The dataset and scalability claims remain under-supported. Appendix A.1 states that approximately 8,300 scenes were selected from 10,000 candidates, but gives no selection criteria, manual-intervention accounting, category distribution, or systematic quality audit. Input-asset provenance and redistribution permissions are unspecified. Runtime, API cost, and refinement-frequency statistics are also missing, despite the pipeline requiring multiple image and mesh generations.

Reproducibility and methodological detail need improvement. Missing details include the SDF construction and resolution, safety margin, mesh sampling, optimization settings, agent stopping threshold, and full prompting/view-selection procedure. The abstract's release link is unfinished. Under the default Algorithms/General assessment, the originality lies mainly in integrating established components; the incomplete controls and implementation details therefore materially weaken the acceptance case.
